title: Boss: the returns platform design review
summary: A design-review ticket: size the log, decide with a matrix that admits when it is close, write the ADR, and generate it end to end.

steps.title: ARCH-57: messaging backbone for the returns platform
body: The returns platform goes live in March. Requirements gathered from the teams:
- return events from 3 storefronts, **4,000 msg/s at peak** (Black Friday), 6 consuming teams (refunds, stock,
- analytics needs **30 days of replay**; refunds need **per-return ordering**;
- label-printing jobs take 2 to 4 minutes each and must be retried individually;
- everything runs on Azure; two engineers have run RabbitMQ before, nobody has run Kafka;
- a refunds consumer handles about 500 msg/s; the candidate log allows 1,000 msg/s per partition.
1. Size the partitions for the event stream with 50% headroom.
2. A scoring function that says which option wins, and says so when the margin is too small to matter.
3. The ADR in the team's Markdown format.
4. One function that produces the ADR from the matrix and the numbers, so the review can rerun it live.

steps.title: 1. Size the partitions
prompt: Write `int PartitionsFor(int peakPerSec, int perConsumerPerSec, int perPartitionPerSec, int headroomPercent)`:
- `target` = `peakPerSec` plus `headroomPercent` percent, **rounded up** to a whole message per second;
- you need enough partitions for the consumers to keep up (`target / perConsumerPerSec`) **and** for each partition's
own limit (`target / perPartitionPerSec`), each rounded up;
- return the larger of the two, and at least 1.
```text
PartitionsFor(4000, 500, 1000, 50)  →  12     (6,000/s target: 12 consumers, 6 partitions' worth of limit)
Use integer arithmetic (no floating point), and watch for overflow on large inputs.
starter: int PartitionsFor(int peakPerSec, int perConsumerPerSec, int perPartitionPerSec, int headroomPercent)
solution: int PartitionsFor(int peakPerSec, int perConsumerPerSec, int perPartitionPerSec, int headroomPercent)
hints: Round up with integers: `(a + b - 1) / b`.
template: Dojo.Eq("no traffic still needs one partition", 1, PartitionsFor(0, 500, 1000, 50));
Dojo.Eq("large numbers do not overflow", 4500, PartitionsFor(2_000_000_000, 1_000_000, 1_000_000, 125));

steps.title: 2. Decide, and admit when it is close
prompt: Write `string Decide(Dictionary<string, int> weights, Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, int>> scores, Dictionary<string, int> minimums)`.
Score and exclude exactly as in `Rank` (weighted sum, missing = 0, knock-outs by minimum; rank by score, then name). Then:
- nothing survives → `"no option meets the must-haves"`
- one survives → `"{name} ({score}), the only option that meets the must-haves"`
- otherwise, with the top two `a` and `b`: if `a`'s lead is **less than 10% of `a`'s score**
(`(sa - sb) * 10 < sa`) → `"{a} ({sa}) narrowly over {b} ({sb}): decide on team skills and ops cost"`,
else `"{a} ({sa}) over {b} ({sb})"`.
starter: string Decide(Dictionary<string, int> weights, Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, int>> scores, Dictionary<string, int> minimums)
solution: string Decide(Dictionary<string, int> weights, Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, int>> scores, Dictionary<string, int> minimums)
if (ranked.Count == 0) return "no option meets the must-haves";
if (ranked.Count == 1) return $"{a.Name} ({a.Score}), the only option that meets the must-haves";
? $"{a.Name} ({a.Score}) narrowly over {b.Name} ({b.Score}): decide on team skills and ops cost"
hints: Filter with `minimums.All(m => o.Value.GetValueOrDefault(m.Key) >= m.Value)`, then project to `(Name, Score)`.
Compare with integers: `(sa - sb) * 10 < sa` means the lead is under 10%.
template: var dojoScores = new Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, int>>

Dojo.Eq("a close call is called close", "event-hubs (32) narrowly over rabbitmq-streams (30): decide on team skills and ops cost", Decide(dojoWeights, dojoScores, new Dictionary<string, int> { ["replay"] = 3 }));
Dojo.Eq("a clear winner", "event-hubs (32) over kafka-on-vms (26)", Decide(dojoWeights, dojoScores, new Dictionary<string, int> { ["replay"] = 5 }));
Dojo.Eq("only one survives", "service-bus (25), the only option that meets the must-haves", Decide(dojoWeights, dojoScores, new Dictionary<string, int> { ["ordering"] = 5 }));
Dojo.Eq("nothing survives", "no option meets the must-haves", Decide(dojoWeights, dojoScores, new Dictionary<string, int> { ["replay"] = 5, ["retry"] = 5 }));

steps.title: 3. Write the ADR
prompt: Write `string Adr(int number, string title, string context, string decision, List<string> consequences, List<string> rejected)`
that returns the team's ADR Markdown, lines joined with `"\n"`:
```text
# ADR-{number}: {title}
Status: Proposed
## Context
{context}
## Decision
{decision}
## Consequences
- {each consequence}
## Alternatives considered
- {each rejected option}
An empty `consequences` or `rejected` list is written as a single `- none` line. No trailing newline.
starter: string Adr(int number, string title, string context, string decision, List<string> consequences, List<string> rejected)
solution: string Adr(int number, string title, string context, string decision, List<string> consequences, List<string> rejected)
hints: Build a `List<string>` of lines and `string.Join("\n", lines)` at the end.
template: "# ADR-57: Messaging backbone for the returns platform",
"- retry topics are ours to build",
}), Adr(57, "Messaging backbone for the returns platform", "4,000 msg/s peak, 30-day replay.", "Use Azure Event Hubs.",
new List<string> { "replay for every team", "retry topics are ours to build" }, new List<string> { "service-bus (score 30)" }));
Dojo.Eq("empty lists become none", string.Join("\n", new[]
"# ADR-58: Label jobs", "", "Status: Proposed", "", "## Context", "c", "", "## Decision", "d", "", "## Consequences", "- none", "", "## Alternatives considered", "- none",
}), Adr(58, "Label jobs", "c", "d", new List<string>(), new List<string>()));

steps.title: 4. Generate the ADR from the numbers
prompt: Put it together so the review can change a weight and rerun. `PartitionsFor` and `Adr` from the previous steps are
already in the editor. Write

`string Recommend(Dictionary<string, int> weights, Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, int>> scores, Dictionary<string, int> minimums, int peakPerSec, int perConsumerPerSec, int perPartitionPerSec)`:
- rank and exclude exactly as before; if nothing survives return `"no option meets the must-haves"`;
- `n = PartitionsFor(peakPerSec, perConsumerPerSec, perPartitionPerSec, 50)`;
- return `Adr(57, "Messaging backbone for the returns platform", context, decision, consequences, rejected)` with
- `context` = `"Peak {peakPerSec} msg/s with 50% headroom. Must-haves: {list}."` where the list is
`"{criterion} >= {minimum}"` items ordered by criterion (ordinal) joined with `", "`, or `none`;
- `decision` = `"Use {winner}, sized for {n} partitions and consumers."`;
- `consequences` = `["weighted score {winnerScore}", "{n} consumers needed at peak"]`;
- `rejected` = the other survivors in rank order as `"{name} (score {score})"`, then the excluded options by name as
`"{name} (excluded: {criterion} {score} < {minimum})"`, with the first failing criterion in ordinal order.
